criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: Names a specific deadline (May 29), three bases, 4,700 acres, two named utilities, and a hard supply constraint in two sentences. At 223 chars the hook lands just past the ~210 'see more' cutoff, meaning the second sentence (the most damning payload) may sit behind the fold on mobile. The first sentence alone carries enough noun/verb/stake to earn a click, but the minor truncation risk keeps this from a 10.

criteria.name: Industry relevance
criteria.notes: Every story links an Alaska angle to a sector consequence. Minor deduction: the MOU story explicitly carries no capital and the right-to-repair business consequence for Alaska specifically is narrower than the other four stories.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Specifics in every paragraph and often in every sentence: acreage, bases, utility names, Hilcorp contract expiry year, ADN cite, hearing dates, session-end deadline, vehicle weight threshold, named opponents, Senate vote tally, named companies, sector job count, percentage declines, absolute position losses, MOU term length, senator name, research center acronyms.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: All five stories in the lineup carry primary or multi-outlet sourcing. Dropped stories (S4, S7) were excluded precisely because they failed this bar. No unsourced claims detected.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Closely matches post_001 style: analytical, position-taking, structural framing of the false dichotomy (chips-and-models read vs. gas molecules and statutory clocks). One minor drift: 'The labor side is worse than the headlines suggest' edges toward newsletter cadence. No banned phrases, no emojis.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: v2 trim: 2773 chars total (under LinkedIn's 3000 cap), 475 body words. Juneau paragraph collapsed from 5 sentences to 4; opposition roster compressed. All five stories preserved. v1 was 3870 chars (870 over cap) and scored 8 here. Holds back from 10 only because the Juneau paragraph is still the densest block in the piece.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Closes with a conditional question tying the two main structural tensions to the May 29 bid date: genuinely debatable, names the operative conditions, no generic prompt, no rhetorical softener.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: A CFO, program manager, or allocator can immediately revisit at least four decisions this week: bid/no-bid on the May 29 DAF lease, power-supply risk modeling, AV fleet planning against HB 217's May 20 cliff, and SB 111 compliance planning.
